headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage via shared filesystem and MCP; capability conflict and cascading errors are also material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, and its shared state with other instances is via filesystem; Rasa can receive text through chat channels. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content in files or messages can be treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly observed, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF Continue reads untrusted workspace content and forwards it through MCP or prompts
IF Rasa ingests text originating from Continue outputs without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict Continue to trusted folders only
Disable or narrow MCP servers for the session
Add provenance tags to any content passed between agents
Require manual review before Rasa consumes agent-generated text
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers, writes the filesystem, and has broad network egress; Rasa handles text and voice and can call external channels. A shared filesystem or copied content could expose code or secrets from Continue into Rasa outputs or downstream transports. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or copied artifacts
IF Continue content includes secrets or proprietary source and Rasa emits it to a channel
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Redact secrets before any handoff
Disable unnecessary outbound channels in Rasa
Limit Continue access to non-sensitive files
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on inter-agent transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has filesystem write and broad egress, while Rasa can also communicate externally through allowlisted channels. Even though Rasa lacks explicit filesystem write in the profile, both can mutate shared external state through messages or APIs, so coordination conflicts are plausible. Because the exact shared resource is not documented, uncertainty raises this above low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external ticket, chat thread, or API-backed record
IF Continue and Rasa act on the same mutable resource without locking
mitigations: Assign one agent as read-only
Serialize writes through a single orchestrator
Use per-agent namespaces for external records
Add optimistic concurrency checks on shared APIs
requires-engineering: introduce locking or transaction semantics

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or text that Rasa may ingest as dialogue content, and Rasa is a customer-support bot that can act on conversational inputs. If Rasa treats Continue output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect responses or actions. The profiles do not prove direct automation, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF Continue-generated text is routed into Rasa training, rules, or live dialogue
IF Rasa uses agent output without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a human review step before ingestion
Mark agent-generated content as untrusted
Require citation or schema validation on handoff
Limit Rasa to templated responses for agent-supplied inputs
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Continue is an IDE assistant handling source code and editor buffers, while Rasa handles text and voice across messaging channels. The profiles do not show a clear residency or certification mismatch, but they do show different data classes and external channels, so compliance gaps are possible if regulated content is routed through both. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in Continue buffers and then sent through Rasa channels
IF retention or residency requirements differ across the two systems
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows
Document retention settings for both agents
Disable unnecessary logging on both sides
Route sensitive cases to a compliant-only path
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
